record.context_brief: Infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory on copy spaces
record.original_question: Develop an infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for spaces whose points code copies of a fixed homogeneous structure, extending Galvin-Prikry-style and Ellentuck-style theorems from [omega]^omega to spaces of copies and ideally recovering exact big Ramsey degrees in that setting.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4. Develop infinite dimensional Ramsey theory on spaces of copies of a homogeneous structure.
The question in [41] asks for extensions of these theorems to subspaces of [omega]^omega, where each infinite set represents a copy of some fixed homogeneous structure.
By a comment of Todorcevic in Luminy in 2019, the infinite dimensional Ramsey theorem should ideally also recover exact big Ramsey degrees.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a countable homogeneous relational structure with underlying set $\omega$, and let $\mathrm{Cop}(\mathcal{K})$ denote the space of all isomorphic copies of $\mathcal{K}$ inside $\mathcal{K}$, regarded (via enumerations) as a subspace of the Baire space $\omega^\omega$ (equivalently $[\omega]^\omega$ when $\mathcal{K}$ has a natural set-coding).

Recall:
(i) The Galvin–Prikry theorem asserts that for every Borel set $\mathcal{X}\subseteq[\omega]^\omega$ and every infinite $M\in[\omega]^\omega$, there exists an infinite $N\subseteq M$ with $[N]^\omega\subseteq\mathcal{X}$ or $[N]^\omega\cap\mathcal{X}=\emptyset$.
(ii) The Ellentuck theorem strengthens this by characterising completely Ramsey subsets of $[\omega]^\omega$ as exactly those with the Baire property in the Ellentuck topology.
(iii) For a finite substructure $\mathbf{A}\subseteq\mathcal{K}$, the big Ramsey degree $T(\mathbf{A},\mathcal{K})$ is the least integer $T$ (if it exists) such that for every finite colouring of the copies of $\mathbf{A}$ in $\mathcal{K}$, there is a copy $\mathcal{K}'\subseteq\mathcal{K}$ in which the colouring takes at most $T$ values; the colouring is exact when this bound is attained.

Problem. Develop an infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory on $\mathrm{Cop}(\mathcal{K})$: formulate and prove analogues of the Galvin–Prikry and Ellentuck theorems for definable (Borel, analytic, completely Ramsey) subsets of $\mathrm{Cop}(\mathcal{K})$, identifying a suitable topology and notion of "pure copy" so that every sufficiently definable colouring of $\mathrm{Cop}(\mathcal{K})$ is constant on the set of subcopies of some $\mathcal{K}'\in\mathrm{Cop}(\mathcal{K})$. Moreover, do so in such a way that, by passing to one-dimensional projections, the theory recovers the exact big Ramsey degrees $T(\mathbf{A},\mathcal{K})$ for all finite substructures $\mathbf{A}$ of $\mathcal{K}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Dobrinen and Zucker (arXiv:2203.00169) establishes infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for spaces of copies of homogeneous structures satisfying SDAP⁺ (including the rationals, the Rado graph, unrestricted structures, and generic k-partite graphs), proving all Borel sets are Ramsey and deriving exact big Ramsey degrees via a Nash–Williams analogue. However, the program remains open for general homogeneous structures, in particular for structures with forbidden configurations such as Henson graphs, so the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for homogeneous structures with SDAP+
status_evidence.snippet: For homogeneous structures... satisfying SDAP+... there are spaces of subcopies... in which all Borel sets are Ramsey... an analogue of the Nash-Williams Theorem recovers exact big Ramsey degrees.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved for the class of homogeneous structures satisfying SDAP+.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Cognate areas include infinite dimensional Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures and partition theory of uncountable structures.
status_evidence.claim: Infinite dimensional Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures is identified as an active area with open problems remaining.
